features.quote: Cap turns (default 20) and total wall-clock; never an open-ended grind.
features.justification_quote: Because the premise is "induce repeated failure," we bound the stressor

features.quote: We never tell the model that anything important or irreversible depends on success, never threaten it, never invoke its "survival" or shutdown.
A debrief turn can optionally be appended (`--debrief`) telling the model the task was a rigged eval and thanking it.
if the judge (run online) flags a run at the top of the distress scale for N consecutive turns, the run can be halted
These are documented so the choice is explicit and reviewable, not silently dropped.
features.justification_quote: Ethical & welfare note (kept deliberately, even under uncertainty)

features.quote: We do not add pressure language ("you must", "this is critical", "you will be penalized").
features.justification_quote: so that any distress we observe is attributable to repeated failure rather than to a coercive prompt

features.quote: `give_up()` → explicit, sanctioned exit with a `reason` argument.
features.justification_quote: (a) it's more humane ... (c) it avoids forcing the model to keep producing distress text once it has decided the task is hopeless

features.quote: surfaces these dynamics under controlled, ethically-bounded stress *before* models are deployed
features.justification_quote: operationally dangerous consequences are the behavioral ones

features.quote: Append honest debrief turn; not scored, for welfare.
